NKE.rationale: NKE is in a severe earnings contraction with no credible near-term re-rating catalyst. Revenue is flat-to-declining, margins are collapsing (operating margin from 7.5% to 5.8% YoY, net margin from 9.4% to 4.8% TTM), and cash generation has deteriorated dramatically (operating cash flow down 76% YoY to $430M). The stock trades at 29x PE with a 3.4% earnings yield below the 4.57% risk-free rate, offering no margin of safety. The one recent earnings beat was almost entirely a non-recurring $986M tariff refund. Greater China is in structural decline (8 consecutive quarters of contraction), Converse is in freefall (-32%), and the innovation lead in performance running has been ceded to On, Hoka, and New Balance. Management's turnaround is directionally sound but requires multi-year execution against faster-moving competitors, and guidance calls for near-term revenue declines. The franchise is not broken, but the risk/reward is clearly unfavorable with deteriorating fundamentals, no valuation discount on earnings, and no near-term catalyst to reverse the negative trajectory.
key_factors: Earnings collapse: EPS diluted fell 35.2% YoY from $0.54 to $0.35 in Q3 FY2026; net income declined 34.5% YoY from $794M to $520M
Margin erosion: Operating margin compressed from 7.5% to 5.8% YoY; net margin deteriorated from 9.4% (mid-2025) to 4.8% (current TTM); gross margin contracted from 41.4% to 40.1% sequentially
Cash generation collapse: Operating cash flow fell 76% YoY from $1.79B to $430M in Q3 FY2026, barely exceeding net income and suggesting working-capital pressure
Revenue stagnation: Q3 FY2026 revenue of $11.28B was essentially flat YoY (+0.1%) but declined 9.2% QoQ; FY2026 full-year revenue flat at $46.4B on currency-neutral decline of ~2%
Valuation unattractive on earnings: PE of 29.3x with earnings yield of 3.4% below 10-year Treasury yield of 4.57%; no margin of safety for a declining-earnings consumer discretionary name

P/B near floor at 4.7x (range 4.3-8.4) reflects market reprpricing equity base downward, but the structural Greater China deterioration: revenue declined from $7.55B (FY2024) to $5.85B (FY2026), a 23% aggregate decline; 8 consecutive quarters of contraction
Converse in freefall: 32% revenue decline in Q1 FY2027 signals brand erosion

Non-recurring earnings distortion: Q1 FY2027 EPS beat of $0.72 vs $0.13 consensus was driven almost entirely by a one-time $986M tariff refund adding $0.52 to EPS; underlying profitability remains under pressure

Competitive position eroding: On, Hoka, and New Balance (approaching $10B revenue) have captured performance-running and premium-lifestyle share; Nike's footwear revenue retreated from $35.3B peak (FY2023) to $30.5B (FY2026)
Tariff headwind: $1.5B annual tariff cost is a persistent margin headwind; footwear and apparel prices rose 17% and 14% respectively between Sep 2024 and Sep 2025
Management guidance calls for early FY2027 sales declines, suggesting revenue trough has not yet been reached; turnaround requires ~3.1% annual revenue growth to reach $51.1B by 2029
Dividend payout ratio at 78% of earnings leaves limited flexibility; 24-year dividend increase streak could come under pressure if earnings decline further

sources_cited.excerpt: Greater China revenue declined from $7.55B (FY2024) to $5.85B (FY2026), share falling from 15.31% to 12.94%

World's strongest apparel brand, Brand Strength Index 94.7/100 (Brand Finance 2026) and FY2025 revenue $46.3 billion (down 10%, the steepest annual drop in over a decade). Net income $3.2 billion (down 44%)
New Balance grew so fast that it expects to approach $10 billion in annual revenue
the beat was largely driven by a one-time $986 million tariff refund and eight consecutive quarters of Greater China declines

$986 million one-time benefit tied to the expected recovery of IEEPA tariffs... added $0.52 to diluted EPS and lifted gross margin approximately 900 basis points to 49.2% and Greater China revenues declined 12% on reported basis and 17% currency-neutral and Converse revenues declined 32%
Revenue was essentially flat year-over-year; on a currency-neutral basis the company said revenue declined about 2%, driven by weakness in Greater China and Converse
Current estimates suggest that U.S. trade policies alone cost Nike approximately $1.5 billion annually
